summary: Round r1 (restricted network). Located 19 leads on data-centre power and connectivity requirements (IEA Energy and AI 2025 and its 2026 update, Masanet et al. Science 2020, Uptime Institute 2025 survey) and on Nepal's supply side (NEA Annual Report FY2024/25, ITU DataHub bandwidth, NTA IT policy 2023, NITC/GIDC). No values retrieved; all empirical items pending. Design: assess three facility archetypes separately and test Nepal's firm dry-season power, transmission and international route diversity rather than monsoon surplus. News reports indicate Nepal lacks a data-centre regulatory framework; unverified.

findings.claim: Research design: data-centre requirements are assessed for three archetypes separately, because requirements differ by orders of magnitude and must not be pooled: (a) enterprise/colocation facility serving domestic demand, (b) regional colocation/cloud edge serving South Asia, (c) hyperscale or AI-training campus. For each: IT load and facility power (MW), annual energy (GWh), required firmness (dry-season supply, redundancy), PUE, cooling water, international bandwidth and route diversity, latency to demand centres, seismic design and grid-connection lead time.

Hydropower surplus in Nepal is seasonal (monsoon); a data centre needs firm year-round supply. Any 'spill energy' figure cannot be equated with available firm capacity without dry-season balance, storage and import data. This is a methodological constraint, not an empirical claim.
Global data-centre electricity consumption (TWh, latest historical year) and IEA projections to 2030/2035 by case, and AI-focused share.
findings.period: Calendar years 2024-2035 (IEA); publication April 2025 and 2026 update
findings.note: Record in GWh (units.py has no TWh). Keep IEA 2025 and 2026 vintages separately and compare with Masanet et al. 2020 bottom-up series.

findings.claim: Typical facility power (MW) and PUE by archetype (enterprise, colocation, hyperscale, AI campus).
findings.note: IEA chapter and Uptime survey; Uptime is an industry survey (lower grade). PUE unit: ratio.

findings.claim: Nepal installed capacity, peak demand, wet- and dry-season energy balance, exports/imports and spilled/curtailed energy.
findings.note: Requires NEA Annual Report FY2024/25; secondary figures in news (L15, L16) must not be used. Coordinate with 05A/22C.

findings.claim: Nepal international internet bandwidth (lit and used), and number/diversity of international routes (India and China).
findings.note: ITU DataHub; route diversity requires NTA reports (not located in r1). Units.py lacks a bandwidth unit (Mbit/s) - raise with 00A.

findings.claim: Nepal regulatory status for data centres (licensing, power tariff category, data-localisation rules, government cloud).
findings.note: Only secondary news located; primary MoIC/NTA/ERC documents needed.

data_gaps: NTA annual report / MIS on international gateways, route diversity and transit capacity not located. The session-wide WebSearch budget was exhausted during this round; data-source hosts and reference hosts (itu.int, nist.gov, wikipedia.org, arxiv.org) returned EGRESS_BLOCKED to WebFetch.
Electricity Regulatory Commission tariff schedule for data-centre-type loads not located.
Seismic design requirements (Nepal National Building Code) for Tier III facilities not located.
Semiconductor supply and export-control documents (X27) not located in r1; 19B holds primary responsibility.
Peer-reviewed data-centre water-use review (Lei, Lu, Shehabi, Masanet 2025, Resources, Conservation and Recycling) identified by citation only; URL not located.
units.py has GWh and NPR_per_kWh/USD_per_kWh but no TWh or bandwidth (Mbit/s) unit; IEA values will be stored as GWh; bandwidth needs a unit addition.

assumptions.text: Facility archetypes are assessed separately; no pooled 'data-centre requirement' is reported.
Only firm (dry-season-available) supply counts toward data-centre feasibility.
assumptions.basis: engineering requirement for continuous loads; to be confirmed with NEA seasonal data

challenges.text: Coordinate on X32: IEA data-centre demand projections affect regional electricity demand and hence Nepal's India/Bangladesh export market; keep the two effects distinct.
Please provide NEA FY2024/25 seasonal balance and curtailment data; 24B will not use news-reported spill figures.
Add a bandwidth unit code (Mbit/s or Gbit/s); IEA TWh values will be stored as GWh; add catalog ids for Nepal Telecommunications Authority and Electricity Regulatory Commission.
Red-team: data-centre-hub narratives in Nepal media rely on monsoon surplus; check any strategy that assumes data-centre exports against dry-season firmness and route-diversity constraints.

uncertainty: High. No values retrieved. Global demand projections vary strongly across IEA cases and vintages and across bottom-up academic estimates; Nepal supply-side data are FY-based while international series are calendar year; regulatory status is known only from news. Nepal feasibility cannot be assessed in r1.

data_centre_requirements.question: What power and connectivity do data centres require, and could Nepal meet them?
data_centre_requirements.answer_r1: Pending. Requirements (power, firmness, PUE, bandwidth) are to be taken from IEA Energy and AI (2025, 2026 update) with Masanet et al. (Science 2020) as methodological comparator and Uptime 2025 as industry survey; Nepal supply side from NEA Annual Report FY2024/25 and ITU bandwidth data. Whether Nepal could meet them cannot be answered in r1: it depends on dry-season firm supply, transmission, international route diversity and a regulatory framework, none of which has retrieved data. Secondary sources suggest no data-centre framework exists (unverified).

feasibility_test.method: For each archetype compare required firm MW and GWh with NEA dry-season surplus and transmission headroom; compare required international capacity/route diversity with ITU/NTA data; list binding constraint(s). No conclusion until data retrieved.

proven_vs_speculative.proven: Data-centre energy intensity and PUE are measured quantities (IEA, Uptime, peer-reviewed).
proven_vs_speculative.speculative: AI-campus demand projections are scenario-dependent (IEA cases); Nepal hosting potential is unevidenced.
